_doc: Headwaters source registry - basin-scoped episodic sources (Arkavathi, Cauvery). Schema + design notes: docs/specs/headwaters.md (local). CADENCE + TIER ARE DOCUMENTATION ONLY - decided 2026-07-26. Neither gates polling: every non-ciBlocked entry is fetched on every weekly run whatever its declared cadence (48 HTTP requests per CI run across ~26 hosts). Deliberate. (1) Cadence is a CLAIM and claims are wrong - CPCB is 'yearly' and shipped a mid-year Yamuna-only file, BBMB was recorded frozen and had resumed, CHIRPS looked daily and publishes monthly; gating polls on a declared cadence inherits every such error and stops looking at exactly the source that surprised you. (2) A conditional check is a check that can silently stop - the WRIS 'green for 39 days while ingesting nothing' bug lives in skip logic. (3) Interval scheduling is maintenance overhead for no real saving at this volume. Cadence earns its place at REVIEW time instead: it tells you whether a detection is plausible - a 'yearly' source producing a new edition three weeks after the last is itself a signal.

sources.refreshMethod: scripts/refresh-arkavathi-mpr.ts (--status / --extract / --diff), driven by the headwaters-refresh skill
playbook: Collected vs generated: MPR solid-waste tables interleave 'Current MSW Generation' and 'Quantity of MSW generated'; repo reads generated=40, collected=35, processed=15 for Ramanagara (June 2025). Never swap the pair (the 35/20-vs-40/15 mix-up).
Priority divergence is content, not conflict: CPCB reads Priority I, KSPCB/MPR reads III-IV. MPR values update only MPR-attributed fields; never overwrite the CPCB priority in prs.json comparisons.
Compound asOf strings ('August 2025 (stretch-wise); April 2026 (STP annexures)') are deliberate - preserve the qualifier structure when bumping.
Consolidated state-annexure editions have contradicted per-stretch reports before; a SCHEMA BREAK edition may be legitimately unusable - skipping it (recorded in notes) is a valid outcome.
Absence in the MPR means 'not recorded in the documents', not 'not happening' - keep the reportingCaveat framing intact.
Year ranges in gaps.json prose ('4.0 MLD (2021-2025)') extend only when the value actually held.
sources.notes: NGT Monthly Progress Reports; file IDs are upload-order, not date-guessable - link-set is the only reliable watch. Pattern scoped to the /ngtmpr/ upload dir (2026-07-21 audit: bare .pdf caught 500+ site-wide links and hit the storage cap). Tables inconsistent report-to-report; prefer per-PRS narrative over consolidated state STP annexures.

sources.notes: Same portal as atlas.json's tngis-generic-viewer-water-bodies, whose note quotes the portal's terms; publication is with TNGIS's permission (the date and form of the permission are to be recorded here). Layers read: admin_master district + taluk boundaries, generic_viewer block_boundary, tnrd panchayat_boundary, sub_basin, microwatersheds, all_water_bodies, reservoir, mines and industry_cad_matched; named tanks arrive through the cauvery-tn ingest. The industry register states no publisher or date: its unit ids follow TNPCB's consent-register format (category letter, registration year 2015 to 2024, office code PND or EDL), and it holds only units matched to a land parcel, so counts are lower bounds. The tngis:, TNGIS_V2: and hilaris: workspaces error (their database does not exist): use generic_viewer:. generic_viewer:raingauge is NOT used - it misplaces stations by tens of km.

Resources: CGWB telemetry 2026-2030 3bd0c6d5-dd9b-4c07-9c60-6410c1c6bd56, Tamil Nadu SW GW telemetry 2026-2030 6857c02f-c77e-4576-b349-3e45aacc1c21, CGWB manual quarterly 2021-2025 21cfbb8e-ac1b-4837-a463-317c05fb6f1b. Traps: telemetry values are negative below ground and some stations flip sign mid-series; 0.0 and 1.0 are placeholders; the District tag follows older district lines (66 Erode-tagged stations plot outside the district, mostly around Dharapuram and Kangayam); the same portal also holds CGWB groundwater QUALITY datasets for Tamil Nadu, not yet used.

sources.notes: Two national CWC layers on NWDP: 'Canal Network' (dataset dd11dfc1-6723-4603-9426-a03e4c8cf50c, SHP resource 75e4b705-44b3-4b4a-a32f-060eeae7b907, 47 MB) and 'Water Resource Project' command areas (dataset a4fde712-4a1f-461b-897a-411ebb29a622, SHP resource 19966957-ccfc-4341-ab11-ca72da5953f4, 41 MB), Lambert conformal conic. Fields: prj_name, can_name, can_type, length_km; command areas carry cca and pot_crted in thousand ha. Checks that held for Erode: the Kalingarayan Channel (91 km) starts 30 m from the OSM Bhavani and both TNPCB real-time canal stations plot 10 m from it. TRAP: three unnamed 'Main Canal' lines filed under 'Kalingarayan Anicut System' lie 20 km east of the channel; they are left out.

Discharge (manual daily): cba07162-d1da-4987-b52e-0c1e2173e287 (1950-2000), fca9df0b-47b1-4f1a-8e59-1b43a8c0ae73 (2001-2025), 38543447-b022-4061-b246-d9c00d134639 (2026-2030). Water quality, chemical: dcb05b97-1ad1-47db-9555-c39938e31309, 0d2370a6-3915-49f2-aa73-bc8bc3613499; biological (BOD, COD, coliform): 6a1e2838-95f2-4878-a1fd-325c618c5b40, b729f83d-044c-43ab-a593-4d82d98b5365. TRAPS: the River column prints the basin for every station; KODUMUDI is printed in CUSECS for 2019-04, 2019-09, 2019-11, 2019-12 and 2020-01 (about 35 times the gauges upstream) and URACHIKOTTAI has one spike (2022-10-25, 154,335): left out, never converted; the conductivity column is labelled mS/cm but holds uS/cm; trace-metal values are implausible (unused). Daily 08:00 reservoir levels for 'Bhavani Sagar Dam' and 'Mettur Reservoir' (from 2016) sit in 'River Water Level CWC Cauvery, Manual Hourly': 3e9b3cde-9d04-4c58-af03-4d4a43cc661b (1991-2020), 5af1557b-bbd3-4551-990c-6bea414b702e (2021-2025), 37cba82e-f745-4004-80d2-b05cad65b8e4 (2026-2030); the station name carries a trailing space in some files. Cross-check that held on 2026-09-17: TN agriculture department 53.29 ft of 105 ft at Bhavanisagar = 264.65 m against 264.59 m here; Mettur within 0.3 m. Entry errors (0.92, 860, 3,190 m) and the gauge-zero placeholder (204.222 at Mettur) are dropped by a 25 m band around each reservoir's median.
